messages:
kevin: Hey team — opening my first PR for the onboarding task. Quick questions: which base branch should I target, any required commit message format, and linters/tests I should run locally? Also who do I ping for runtime vs infra reviews?

olivia: Welcome! Use main as the base (we do trunk-based flow). Branch names: feat/KEV-<ticket>-short-desc or fix/ for bugs. Try to keep PRs small (<500 LOC) where possible.

olivia: Our commit style is lightweight but consistent. Example we prefer:
```
runtime(prefix-cache): reduce mem for prefix caching (#KEV-123)
```
Include the ticket id somewhere in the message. Not strict conventional-commits, but scope helps reviewers.

olivia: Locally run: `pre-commit run --all-files`, `make test` (or `./scripts/run_tests.sh`), and `black .` / `yarn format` for formatting. If you edit proto/schema run `make gen` afterwards.

sam: Frontend bits: run `yarn ci-lint` + `yarn test`. CI will run full suite (linters, unit tests, typechecks). If CI fails, fix locally and push.

mike: CODEOWNERS covers runtime/* -> @sam, infra/* -> @mike, docs/* -> @olivia. If your change touches more than one area, add reviewers manually. If unsure, ping the area owner in the PR description.

olivia: Open as a Draft PR if tests take a while. Convert to Ready when CI is green. Merge rules: 2 approvals + green CI + no conflicts = auto-merge. If it's a risky change, mark with `needs-sr` (senior reviewer) or request a canary rollout in the PR body.

kevin: Good to know. Anything special about tests coverage or perf tests for runtime changes?

olivia: We don't gate on global coverage numbers, but add focused unit tests for new logic and edge cases. For perf-sensitive runtime changes include a small benchmark or before/after numbers in the PR description. If it's a FASTPATH change, mention it clearly so infra can run safety checks.

devex-bot: CI started for PR #42 · linux/unit-tests queued · lint queued

kevin: Awesome — thanks! One more tiny Q: preferred PR description template?

olivia: Use the PR template in .github/pull_request_template.md — short summary, motivation, testing done, rollout plan, and owners/cc. Minimal example:
```
Summary: one-line summary
Motivation: why this matters
Testing: unit tests + how you ran them
Rollout: feature flag / canary instructions (if any)
CC: @sam @mike
```

kevin: Perfect. I'll follow that and tag folks. Appreciate the quick help :raised_hands:

sam: Ping me if it's runtime perf-related, happy to take a look early.

mike: And ping me for infra/CI changes. If you touch deploy config, do not merge until I ack.

kevin: Will do. Thanks everyone :wave:
